solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Supporters being rowdy at stadium, initially (4)

indicatorNotes.initially: take each word at its start

blocks.note: the opening letters of the four words

annotation.surface: Football supporters misbehaving at the ground.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Supporters' reads as fans, which the rest of the clue encourages; it is underwear.
annotation.definitionFit: A playful sense: these undergarments exist to give support.

indicatorNotes.some: only part of the following words is used

blocks.note: the answer runs from the end of acupuncture, through can, into the start of tingle

annotation.surface: A patient backing off from acupuncture because the needles tingle.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Withdrawing' looks like pulling out of treatment; it means taking back a statement.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym in the sense of taking back what one said.

indicatorNotes.protecting: the lord wraps round the queen as a bodyguard would

blocks.note: sire = lord, a form of address to a king

annotation.surface: A nobleman guarding the Queen and seeing her home.
annotation.walkthrough: 'protecting' pictures a bodyguard; it only means the lord's letters wrap round hers, split after the first.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: escorting a lady was a squire's duty, and the noun became the verb.

blocks.note: tone = shade of colour; 'with' joins it on

annotation.surface: Choosing the edging and colour for a picture of a butterfly.
annotation.walkthrough: The butterfly is a common yellow European species; the word is better known as sulphur, as in fire and brimstone.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: a pale yellow European butterfly named for its sulphur colour.

annotation.surface: Beating yourself with birch twigs in a sauna, as the Finns do.
annotation.walkthrough: 'possibly' flags that the definition works by example: a sauna is only one kind.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: a sauna is a steam room, one variety of the thing you wash in.

indicatorNotes.out: the letters are put out of order

annotation.surface: A plea to tempt the Conservatives out to vote while the voters are unsure.
annotation.walkthrough: The Tories are Britain's Conservative Party; the political surface hides that 'out' only scrambles the letters.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: unable to make up one's mind.

indicatorNotes.purchasing: to purchase is to take in, so the drinks hold the drink

annotation.surface: Someone delaying the round while they buy more drink.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Holds up' suggests a delay at the bar, and 'purchasing' a round being bought; purchasing only means taking in.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: bears the weight of.

indicatorNotes.losing head: a word that loses its head loses its first letter, the top of it

annotation.surface: Someone who loses their temper, and does it regularly.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Temper' is the verb, as in to temper criticism, so it means soften, not anger.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: frequently, time and again.

indicatorNotes.picked up: heard, as a radio picks up a signal

blocks.note: to net money is to earn it

annotation.surface: A bird caught in a net and lifted out.
annotation.walkthrough: 'net' looks like mesh for catching birds; it is the verb, to clear as profit.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: the white-tailed sea eagle, a crossword favourite.

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 9 letters with the S

annotation.surface: A fickle relative going through changes.
annotation.walkthrough: The apostrophe S is just a letter here, so the fodder has all nine.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: adapting readily, able to turn to anything.

indicatorNotes.emptied: an emptied word has lost its contents, keeping only its shell

blocks.note: a counter is a bar, as in a shop or pub

annotation.surface: A pub brawl breaking out and clearing the bar.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface pictures a bar emptied by a brawl; 'emptied' belongs to 'eruption' instead.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a clash between opposing forces.

blocks.note: the President of Russia, by surname
a two-word phrasal verb for fitted, run together

annotation.surface: A news line about a Russian leader being sworn in.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Russian leader' tempts the solver to take R, the first letter of Russian; here it means the man himself.
annotation.definitionFit: A double definition: the Russian President's surname, and a phrasal verb meaning fitted in place.

annotation.surface: A guard stationed beside the railway line.
annotation.walkthrough: 'posted' reads as stationed on duty, which suits a guard; it means mailed.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a soldier put on watch.

entries.clue: A racket around tenement’s first floor (7)

indicatorNotes.around: the racket goes round the letter
indicatorNotes.first: take the first letter of tenement

annotation.surface: A noisy racket in the ground floor flat of a tenement.
annotation.walkthrough: 'floor' is not the ground floor of the surface but the verb, to knock someone flat with surprise.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym in the verb sense: to leave someone stunned.

entries.clue: Dedication of note about Cambridge University (10)

indicatorNotes.about: the note goes round the university

blocks.note: a note is a comment, a remark
the Massachusetts Institute of Technology stands in Cambridge, Massachusetts

annotation.surface: A dedication written in a book, with a note about Cambridge University.
annotation.walkthrough: Cambridge University points to England, but the one meant is across the Atlantic in Cambridge, Massachusetts.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: devotion to a cause or person.

entries.clue: Bending in empty grasslands for leftovers (9)

indicatorNotes.in: one piece sits inside the other
indicatorNotes.empty: an empty word has lost its contents, leaving only the ends

annotation.surface: Stooping in bare fields to pick up what the harvest left.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is the activity itself: bending in cleared fields for leftover grain.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: what is gathered after the harvest, the scraps left over.

indicatorNotes.wearing: the queen has the crown around her

blocks.note: the crown is the top, or tip

annotation.surface: A royal tour on which the Queen wears her crown.
annotation.walkthrough: 'crown' suggests regalia; here it is the top of something, like the crown of a hill.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a journey away and back.

entries.clue: Guarantee from all to clear off (10)

indicatorNotes.off: something off is wrong or out of place, so the letters are out of order

annotation.surface: A guarantee that everyone is free to leave.
annotation.walkthrough: 'clear off' reads as go away, but 'clear' is fodder and 'off' the instruction.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym in finance: security pledged against a loan.

entries.clue: Fall of rain out in wild (9)

indicatorNotes.wild: something wild is out of control, so the letters are in no set order

annotation.surface: Rain falling outdoors in the wilderness.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Fall of rain' reads as one phrase, rainfall; 'Fall' alone is the definition, a downfall.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym in the downfall sense: collapse into ruin.

blocks.note: status in the eyes of others
one word describes water that is still and a person getting to their feet

annotation.surface: A reputation that keeps on growing.
annotation.walkthrough: 'still rising' reads as continuing to climb; each word is a sense of the answer: standing water is still, and standing up is rising.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: one's position in others' esteem, as in good standing.

entries.clue: Elope with single partner being proper (10)

annotation.surface: Running off with your one true love to make things respectable.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Leg it' is British slang for run off, which covers eloping.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: lawful and above board.

blocks.note: the surface wants a city Italy once governed from; the setter means money it once used
the question mark warns that capital is being used in an unexpected sense

annotation.surface: A quiz question about which city Italy used to govern from.
annotation.walkthrough: 'capital' wants a city, with Turin or Florence as the answer; it is money, and Italy's old currency gave way to the euro in 2002.
annotation.definitionFit: A crossword pun: capital as money, so Italy's currency before the euro.

entries.clue: Stop, please, not entirely getting upset! (6)

indicatorNotes.not entirely: the answer takes only parts of the words

blocks.note: the answer runs from the second letter of the first word to the middle of please

annotation.surface: A plea to stop before someone gets upset.
annotation.walkthrough: 'upset' reads as distressed; here it is the verb, to knock over.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym in the knocking-over sense of upset, not the distressed one.

entries.clue: Stone jar keeping cool in recess (7)

indicatorNotes.keeping: the jar holds the other piece

blocks.note: to grate is to jar, on the nerves

annotation.surface: A stone jar kept cool in an alcove.
annotation.walkthrough: 'jar' is the verb, to irritate, and 'recess' is not an alcove but a retreat: a word in recess goes backwards.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: a hard igneous rock, one kind of stone.

entries.clue: Country is source of Russian river (5)

indicatorNotes.source of: a word's source is where it starts

blocks.note: the Ural, a river through Russia and Kazakhstan

annotation.surface: A country whose rivers rise in Russia.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Country' looks like a nation; it is the adjective, as in country life.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym in the adjective sense: of the countryside rather than the town.

annotation.surface: A tautology: an African country is African.
annotation.walkthrough: 'African' appears twice; the first belongs to the country in the wordplay, the second is the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: a person from Somalia on the Horn of Africa.

indicatorNotes.Endless: a word without an end has lost its last letter

annotation.surface: A boss who makes staff work without end.
annotation.walkthrough: 'boss' reads as manager; it is a raised knob, as on a shield.
annotation.definitionFit: A less familiar sense: a boss is a raised ornamental knob, like those on a shield or belt.

annotation.surface: A fun day out at the swimming pool.
annotation.walkthrough: 'pool' is the swimming kind in the surface; it is money put together.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym in the money sense: contributions gathered together.

indicatorNotes.around: to turn around is to face the other way, so the letters run backwards
indicatorNotes.oddly: the odd-numbered letters, first and third, are kept

blocks.note: S, I: the first and third letters of soil

annotation.surface: Tree trunks rotting in the soil.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Trunks' suggests trees; it means human bodies from neck to hips, with the Italian-style plural.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: the trunk of the body, in the plural.

indicatorNotes.heart: the heart of a word is its middle

annotation.surface: A lover making jokes while getting dressed.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Sweetheart' reads as a lover; split it into sweet and heart and it gives the middle of sweet.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: fitting someone out with gear.

annotation.surface: A happy pursuit that involves hugging a blonde.
annotation.walkthrough: 'blonde' reads as a person being hugged; it is the adjective, fair-haired, so light.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: very happy.

indicatorNotes.Backing: to back is to move in reverse, so the word is read from its end

blocks.note: an ante is a stake in poker

annotation.surface: Betting on a horse, an unpredictable mount.
annotation.walkthrough: 'mount' suggests a horse, and 'Backing' a bet; the mount is a Sicilian volcano whose eruptions come unannounced.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: an active volcano in Sicily, unpredictable in its eruptions.
